purpose: Romiplostim is used to raise platelet counts in adults and children who have a blood condition called immune thrombocytopenia (ITP), where the immune system destroys platelets too quickly. Low platelets can cause easy bruising and dangerous bleeding. This medication helps your body make more platelets to keep you safer.
how_it_works: Your body naturally makes a protein called thrombopoietin that tells your bone marrow to produce platelets. Romiplostim mimics that natural signal and attaches to the same receptor, telling your bone marrow to ramp up platelet production. Think of it like pressing the gas pedal on your platelet factory so your counts stay at a safe level.
common_side_effects: Headache, dizziness, bruising, joint or muscle pain, stomach pain, nausea, tiredness, and runny nose are the most common side effects. Some people may also notice swelling in the arms or legs.
warnings: Important: This medicine can rarely cause bone marrow changes or scar tissue over time, so your doctor will monitor you closely. There is also a small risk of blood clots, especially if your platelet count goes too high. Do not stop this medication suddenly without talking to your doctor, as your platelet count could drop dangerously low. This medicine is only available through a special restricted program called the Nplate NEXUS Program.
typical_dosing: Romiplostim is given as a weekly injection under the skin (subcutaneous shot), usually by a healthcare provider in a clinic. The starting dose is typically 1 microgram per kilogram of your body weight, and your doctor will adjust the dose week by week based on your platelet count results. The goal is to find the lowest dose that keeps your platelets at a safe level.
